title: Customer capacity activation timeline and fallbacks - Feb 2030
content:
Summary:
This working sheet defines the end-to-end activation cadence for per-contract dedicated GPU reservations, the staged ramp (validation -> pilot -> production), utilization targets, and concrete fallback options if capacity or region constraints occur. The goal is a repeatable play for the next 8 contracts to reduce lead time from contract signature to production traffic to <= 6 weeks for standard skus (A100/H100).

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Dedicated reservations (monthly/annual committed capacity) that require: private routing, customer tenant isolation, and per-contract placement.
- GPU SKUs considered: A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100-80GB (NVIDIA).
- Regions supported in runbook: us-west1, us-east4, europe-west2, asia-southeast1.
- Target steady-state utilization: 65% average (60-75% range) for economic efficiency while leaving headroom for bursts and KV cache growth.
- We reserve a 10% buffer per customer during first 4 weeks of production to reduce risk.

Activation timeline (canonical 6-week ramp):
- Week 0: Contract executed + commercial signal -> Capacity request created in internal RDW system. ASSIGNEE: Solutions Eng (S. Martinez).
- Week 1: Internal capacity validation and region feasibility check. Confirm SKU availability across requested regions. ASSIGNEE: Capacity Ops (E. Li).
- Week 2: Networking & VPC peering scheduled; private plane provisioning started. ASSIGNEE: Private Deployments (R. Kapoor).
- Week 3: Resource pinning and ephemeral test lane deployed. Customer test harness (small replay) run. ASSIGNEE: Eng-SRE (A. Patel).
- Week 4: Pilot traffic (10–20% of volume). Monitor latency, error rates, utilization. Automated rollback criteria defined. ASSIGNEE: Customer Success + Eng-SRE.
- Week 5: Gradual ramp to 50% with 10% buffer preserved. Validate batch behavior and KV cache hit-rate. ASSIGNEE: Platform Engineering.
- Week 6: Full production (expected). Post-activation review and final capacity reconciliation. ASSIGNEE: Capacity Ops.

Per-contract sample table (text representation):
- Contract: ACME-334 | Regions: us-west1 primary, us-east4 failover | SKU: H100-80GB | Reserved GPUs: 24 | Ramp weeks: follow canonical 6-week | Target util: 65% | Buffer: 10% first 4wks
- Contract: NOVA-201 | Regions: europe-west2 primary | SKU: A100-80GB | Reserved GPUs: 12 | Notes: requires sustained KV-cache for chat workloads.

Utilization and capacity math (example):
- Reserved GPUs: 24 H100s. Effective concurrency factors and batching expected to yield 120k tokens/min at 65% util. If observed util dips below 45% for >7 days, flag for reclamation/rightsizing. If util >85% for >3 days, enable immediate burst or revise commit.

Fallback policies (ordered):
1) Cross-region failover: route traffic to customer-designated failover region where reservation exists. Must ensure data residency rules permit.
2) Shared-burst pool: allow short-term burst into shared-hosted pool for latency-sensitive requests (cost premium applies). Triggered when sustained utilization >80% and pilot approvals present.
3) Model degradation: automatically fall back to a smaller quantized variant (e.g., H100 -> A100-quantized) for non-critical routes. Only enabled after customer consent in contract.
4) Queueing/degraded feature set: delay non-real-time requests (batching) and disable optional tooling (reranking) until capacity stabilizes.

Operational checks and monitoring:
- Dashboards: Per-contract utilization, per-region availability, per-model latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), KV cache hit-rate.
- Alerts: Utilization cross thresholds (45% low, 80% high), model error rate spike >2x baseline, region outage detection. Pagering: on-call SRE -> capacity ops.
- Audit: Every activation includes a postmortem checklist and a short RACI doc attached to the contract page in Confluence.

Constraints and common blockers observed in past activations (notes):
- SKU availability mismatch between requested region and reserved hardware windows (fix: propose adjacent region with transit allowance and customer signoff).
- Long lead times for HSM/KMS key setups for Private deployments (fix: kickoff earlier and parallelize networking + KMS tasks).
- Interference from scheduled maint windows (fix: schedule pilot outside maintenance windows; adjust maintenance SLA for committed customers).

Action items (owner - due):
- Finalize activation automation checklist in RDW system - Marco Chen - 2029-11-20
- Add shared-burst billing meter to billing pipeline - Finance/Platform - 2029-12-15
- Create runbook for model degradation policy and opt-in consent template - Product/Legal - 2030-01-10
- Run 2 cross-region failover drills with staging tenants - Eng-SRE - 2030-01-28

Open questions for commercial & legal:
- Can we standardize a 10% buffer window for all 12-month contracts, or should buffer vary by SKU and region?
- What is acceptable maximum latency increase when failing over to shared-burst vs cross-region? Need explicit thresholds for SLO clauses.

Notes and references (working):
- See Confluence runbook for detailed steps and checklist link above.
- Related Jira tickets: JIRA-OPS-4012 (capacity pinning automation), JIRA-SEC-1160 (KMS onboarding delays).
- Slack thread: #capacity-onboards for ad-hoc coordination.

This is an iterative working sheet — expect edits as we complete 3 more activations. Keep comments inline and tag owners for sign-off.
